_note: The committee recommendation is the analyst's judgment, written after reading output/report.md. The app and the memo display this file; the engine does not generate it.
headline: Reject the minimum-volatility optimizer process: allocate 0% of the reserve to it. Rebalance the existing 60/40 holdings only enough to fund the payout reserve.
process_allocation_range: 0% of the $100M reserve (paper-track only; no live capital)
reserve_allocation_text: ACWI 55-60%, AGG 35-40%, BIL 3-5% ($3-5M of T-bills covers the $3.0M twelve-month payout reserve; one-way turnover 3-5%, inside the 25% limit, so no extra committee approval is needed).
why: The process trips two of its own three stop conditions: a 60-month estimation window moves the portfolio 30 points one-way (limit 25%), and the walk-forward 2022 calendar-year loss was -10.8% (limit -10%).

Out of sample (Jan 2012 - Oct 2026, annual December rebalances, costs charged) it returned 6.33% a year versus 7.68% for the 60/40 benchmark, below the 6.5% CPI + 4% hurdle, and was infeasible in 3 of 15 rebalance years.
Its turnover exceeded the 25% S7 limit in 12 of 14 rebalances after the first: the allocation follows the trailing window, not the client.
Today's answer (85% BIL / 15% ACWI) passes every rule only because ACWI's trailing 36-month mean is 20.8% a year; that is the Lab 13 'all-cash D' problem the rules cannot see.

The fallback is not a cure either: the recommended reserve range earned 7.20-7.67% a year over the same holdout but lost 15.3-15.8% in 2022, so the objective and the loss limit cannot both be met on this evidence.

The point-in-time term-spread signal never changed a rebalance (the curve was inverted only in the two years the process had already stopped) and has no reliable monthly edge (t = 0.08 inverted, 1.07 positive).
committee_ask: Vote to reject adoption of the optimizer process (0% allocation; I keep it on a paper track and rerun it each December).
Approve a compliance rebalance of the current reserve to ACWI 55-60% / AGG 35-40% / BIL 3-5%.

Ask the CIO to resolve the mandate conflict before any optimizer is reconsidered: on Jan 2012 - Oct 2026 data none of the five walk-forward strategies met both CPI + 4% and a 10% worst calendar-year loss. Which one gives way?
